title: Loops & Repetition: Iteration & Accumulation
description: Master repetition with for and while loops, control iteration bounds safely, apply the accumulator pattern to calculate totals, and avoid infinite loop and off-by-one errors.

objectives.statement: Construct for loops with correct initialization, condition bounds, and step increments without off-by-one errors.
Apply the accumulator pattern in loops to aggregate counts, sums, or constructed output values.

content.title: The Power of Repetition
content.hook: Writing the same code 1,000 times by hand is tedious and error-prone. Loops allow you to execute a code block any number of times with precision and speed.
content.context: The standard for loop consists of three parts: initialization (let i = 0), condition check (i < limit), and increment (i++). Combining loops with accumulator variables lets you compute aggregates and transform collections.
goals: Understand the 3-part anatomy of a for loop.
Prevent off-by-one errors and infinite loops.
Implement the accumulator pattern to compute totals and sums.

content.title: Anatomy of a for Loop
content.description: for (initialization; condition; increment) -> Initialization runs once -> Condition tested before each step -> Body executes if true -> Increment step -> Repeat until condition is false.

content.prompt: What value will be printed to the console when this script runs?
content.explanation: Iterations: i=1 -> product=1; i=2 -> product=2; i=3 -> product=6; i=4 -> product=24.

content.title: Calculate Even Numbers Sum
content.prompt: Declare `let evenSum = 0;`. Write a for loop that iterates `i` from `1` through `10` (inclusive). Inside the loop, if `i % 2 === 0`, add `i` to `evenSum`.

feedback.correct: Great work! You combined loop bounds with conditional accumulator filtering.
feedback.incorrect: Check that your loop runs from 1 to 10 inclusive and tests i % 2 === 0.

content.question: How many times does the loop body execute in: `for (let i = 0; i < 4; i++)`?
content.explanation: The loop executes for i = 0, 1, 2, 3 (4 total times). When i becomes 4, 4 < 4 is false and the loop terminates.

feedback.correct: Correct! It executes for 0, 1, 2, 3 (4 total iterations).
feedback.incorrect: Remember that i starts at 0 and increments until i < 4 is no longer true.

content.title: Loops & Repetition Mastered
takeaways: A for loop manages initialization, condition checking, and stepping in a clean syntax.
The accumulator pattern collects totals or transformed data across multiple iterations.
Always verify loop bounds (< vs <=) to prevent off-by-one errors.
